proof_nl:
Let y = n t. Since n > 1, we have n > 0. The hypothesis m/n ≤ t < (m+1)/n can therefore be multiplied by n without reversing the inequalities, giving
m ≤ n t < m+1.
That is,
m ≤ y < m+1.
By the defining property of the floor function, an integer q satisfies q = floor(y) exactly when q ≤ y < q+1. Since m is an integer and m ≤ y < m+1, it follows that floor(y) = m. Substituting back y = n t gives floor(n t) = m.
solver_summary: Multiply the interval condition by the positive integer n to obtain m ≤ nt < m+1, then apply the defining property of the floor function.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly derives m <= n t < m+1 from m/n <= t < (m+1)/n using n>0, then applies the defining characterization of floor to conclude floor(n t)=m. This matches the lemma statement exactly and uses only permitted elementary reasoning.
